newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise, bonds weaker, dollar hits new 6-year high.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise, bonds weaker, dollar hits new 6-year high.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed slightly higher on Monday, but the Nasdaq market soared as technology stocks extending their powerful rally.
Bonds drifted lower, while the dollar surged to a new six-year high against the German mark.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 1.16 points at 7,922.98.
The Nasdaq index rose 21.26 points to 1,523.88, extending its streak of consecutive record closes to eight, as investors flocked to the suddenly sizzling tech sector.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,471 to 1,375 on moderate volume of 485 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The tech stocks face a critical series of earnings-related tests this week, with reports due from industry bellwether companies Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp.

"We get Intel tomorrow and Microsoft on Thursday," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management, "and this trend could either break or continue right on, based on what those two companies say."

Intel warned in late May that its second quarter earnings would fall short of earlier forecasts due to product transition issues. Investors have apparently decided the worst is already passed, analysts said.
"Right now, the market is certainly telling us it expects good news," Truicko said.
At the same time tech stocks have shot higher, the Dow has stalled a bit, remaining stuck just below the 8,000 mark since closing at 7,895.81 on July 3.
While analysts are not expecting a stiff blue chip correction, they say the milestone may remain elusive for a while longer, as investors flock to the once again favoured technology group.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 11/32, or $3.4375 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.55 percent to 6.53 percent Friday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The dollar rocketed to almost 1.80 marks, before ending the day at 1.7965 marks, up from 1.7773 late Friday. But it edged lower to 113.96 Japanese yen from 114.00.
Corn and soybean prices soared on fears that hot, dry weather in the Midwest will hurt crop growth as the plants enter a key growth stage.
Corn for post-harvest delivery in December closed up the 12-cent-a-bushel trading limit at $2.49, with corn for July delivery up 10-3/4 cents to close at $2.62-1/4.

Soybeans for post-harvest delivery in November closed 28 cents a bushel higher at $6.21-3/4, just off the 30-cent daily limit. July soybeans, now in a cash delivery period and not subject to limits, closed 33-1/2 cents higher at $8.19.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil prices led other energy markets lower on news that Iraq and the United Nations had agreed to Iraq's new aid distribution plan, moving Iraq a step closer to resuming oil sales.

August crude settled off 34 cents at $18.99 a barrel. Refined products tracked crude lower, with August heating oil ending down 0.68 cent at 51.67 cents a gallon and August gasoline finishing down 0.91 cent a gallon at 58.35 cents.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 rose 57.9 points to 4,857.4. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,228.72, up 353.23 points, or 1.78 percent.
